newsitem.title: UK: OPEC's Salman warns oil price may slip in 4th qtr.
newsitem.headline: OPEC's Salman warns oil price may slip in 4th qtr.

text.p: Rising non-OPEC production, some from delayed North Sea fields, and the resumption of Iraqi crude exports could push oil prices down later this year, OPEC deputy secretary general Ramzi Salman said, OPEC news agency reported.

"It is expected that these delayed fields will come onstream in the fourth quarter, while the timing for Iraqi crude, in the oil for food and medicine deal was also about the same time," Salman told OPECNA in an interview.
"This may lead to a softening of the market, which in turn, would require that OPEC members adhere strictly to their quotas in order to keep prices as firm as possible," Salman said.
He said Iraq's return after six years had already been factored in to the market.
"There will be no shock when Iraq returns to the market because the world and OPEC have already taken this into consideration."

Salman said it was in the interest of OPEC members to observe their output quotas but added that the 11-member group had no means of policing production levels which have consistently overshot official allocations.
"OPEC is not a policeman, has no disciplinary power and no court. We can only assume (members) are honouring their commitments and will abide by them."
OPEC monitors output with a three-man quota compliance committee chaired currently by Iranian minister Gholamrezah Aghazadeh.
